decision: branched prerelease/solid-2 off main and committed the dirty tree's vite-plus work first
why: main's working tree was dirty; separating it keeps the migration diff readable

decision: read the real .d.ts of solid-js 2.0.0-rc.3 and @solidjs/universal 2.0.0-rc.0 instead of trusting the migration guide
why: the guide is prose; the shipped types are the contract
result: confirmed createResource, splitProps, mergeProps, Suspense, ErrorBoundary, Index, SuspenseList all gone

decision: keeping the requested pairing of solid-js rc.3 with @solidjs/universal rc.0
why: universal rc.0 only imports createMemo, createRenderEffect, createComponent, merge, createRoot, untrack, runWithOwner, flatten, flush from solid-js, and rc.3 still exports every one

decision: renderer contract changed: effect and createRenderEffect now take (compute, apply), use is replaced by applyRef and ref, spread gained skipChildren
why: these are the pieces runtime.tsx is built on, so the renderer glue is a rewrite not a rename

decision: rigor set high: build a real test harness before touching source, and baseline it against the Solid 1 code
why: public library, major version, zero existing tests, and the renderer glue rides on runtime contracts a typecheck cannot see

decision: probe says the whole pixi scene graph runs headless in node, no canvas needed
why: means the bulk of the harness is a fast plain node suite; only Application needs a real renderer
evidence: Container, addChildAt, removeFromParent, Text mutate, Graphics, setSize all constructed and mutated fine under node 24

decision: found a latent bug while probing: runtime.tsx builds text with the deprecated new Text(value) form
why: pixi v8 warns on it; the migration is the moment to fix it

decision: compile the tests with universal generate pointed at solid-pixi, not dom generate
why: it exercises solid-pixi's own createComponent/insert/spread/setProp codegen path, which is exactly the surface this migration changes
evidence: '@solidjs/universal README, runtime.tsx already exports the v1 universal export set

decision: wrote 13 scene-graph tests and got them green on solid-js 1.9 before touching any source
why: gives the migration an old-value/new-value check instead of assertions written to fit whatever Solid 2 does

decision: vitest was loading solid-js's server build, so every signal write was a no-op
why: found it with a bare createSignal probe rather than guessing at the 5 failing tests

decision: pinned 'dispose leaves nodes attached to the root' as its own test instead of asserting the tidy behaviour
why: that is what Solid 1 actually does; if rc.0 changes it I want a red test and a deliberate call, not a silent difference

decision: no coverage for the four use* asset hooks
why: Assets.load needs fetch and image decoding, too heavy for the node harness

decision: returned the async accessor itself with progress attached, rather than a tuple or a {data} object
why: refresh, isPending and latest all take the accessor; wrapping it would make every Solid 2 idiom read result.data
result: 3 of 3 designers said drop mutate and refetch; 2 of 3 said attach to the accessor

decision: kept useAssetInit but made its options non-reactive
why: pixi ignores a second Assets.init, so the old MaybeAccessor signature promised a re-run that never happened

decision: dropped the derived debug-name logic from all four hooks
why: it read the source at hook-call top level, which Solid 2 warns on, and it only fed a dev label; callers can pass name in options

decision: the universal ref() helper assumes a ref exists and crashed on every mount
why: caught by the harness, not by the typecheck; replaced with a two-phase render effect that guards and uses applyRef

decision: build was inlining all of pixi.js into a 504 kB bundle
why: build.external is not the key rolldown reads; the error message named build.rolldownOptions.external

decision: aliased solid-pixi to src/runtime.tsx inside the library's own build
why: universal codegen emits imports from moduleName, so the library's own JSX imported itself by package name and rolldown could not resolve it

decision: the browser check caught a crash on every mount: passing a pending async value to a context provider is a hard error, not a suspension
why: typecheck and the node harness both stayed green through it; only a real Application in a real browser surfaced it
result: fixed with a tracked Show read inside the Loading boundary

decision: my first attempt at the removed-API gate passed even with a createResource import injected
why: the name regex anchored on ^ after the braces were sliced off, so it matched nothing; checked the gate by breaking the source on purpose
result: rewrote it and falsified all three gates

decision: falsified the Loading gate check too, by mounting the same ref outside the boundary
why: an assertion that cannot fail is not evidence
result: FAIL when unguarded, PASS when guarded

decision: gave solid-pixi-unsafe its own solid-js 1.9 and vite-plugin-solid devDeps instead of migrating it
why: it was relying on root hoisting for both, so removing them from the root broke its build; declaring them is honest, and migrating it was not asked for

decision: left packages/docs on solid-js 1.9
why: '@astrojs/solid-js has no Solid 2 support, so the docs site cannot follow yet

decision: deleted spread's dynamic-accessor branch instead of porting it to the two-phase effect
why: the universal Renderer type takes props, not an accessor; that branch was solid-pixi's own invention and nothing reachable calls it

decision: ran a three-model design panel on the asset-hook API before writing it
why: it is a one-way door for every consumer of the library and the tuple shape had no Solid 2 equivalent
evidence: judgment, opus and precise read-only designers
result: converged on dropping mutate and refetch

decision: cross-model reviewer flagged setProp arity, a 36-vs-14 test count and a gate blind to multiline imports; all three were wrong
why: checked each against the shipped types and by rerunning, rather than editing code to satisfy the review

decision: reviewer was right that the asset hooks and Application re-init were untested; covered both in the browser
why: the hooks are the biggest API change in the release and had zero coverage

decision: browser check proved the hooks end to end and disproved the re-init worry
why: loads a real PNG over http, suspends under Loading, progress hits 1, green pixels land; renderer and stage identity survive an option change
